personas.story: Dana leads commerce engineering at a home-goods retailer. Her team publishes a profile at /.well-known/ucp with checkout, fulfillment and a Google Pay handler, and keeps its own PSP. The first week, agent orders arrive through AI Mode, and the platform's profile and signature check out on every call. Large furniture orders need a delivery window that their API cannot take, so the checkout returns requires_escalation with a continue_url to the store's own page. Conversion on that path is lower, so she adds a scheduling field to the next release. The merchant-of-record question never comes up: refunds and disputes stay with her team, exactly as before.

personas.story: Ravi runs the shopping agent of a large assistant app. Each store his agent visits has a slightly different profile: one offers cart and checkout with the fulfillment extension, another only cart. His code picks the highest common version, prunes an extension when none of its parent capabilities is shared (fulfillment needs checkout or catalog), and sends the platform profile in UCP-Agent on every call. One night a store times out on complete. The agent polls Get Checkout, sees complete_in_progress, and waits instead of resending. The order shows up as completed an hour later, with one charge. Ravi adds the case to his test suite and moves on to identity linking.

personas.story: Ana works on a wallet team that wants its button in agent checkouts. She writes a handler spec under the wallet's own domain, because dev.ucp is reserved, and a schema for the business config. Businesses add the handler to their profile with their merchant id. Platforms run the handler, get a token bound to the merchant and session, and pass it in payment.instruments. Ana never sees the checkout itself, and the business never sees the card number. Her open question is AP2: the extension lets a wallet sign mandates with a key bound to a payment credential, but she has not found a deployment that does it yet.

personas.story: Jonas manages agentic payments at a PSP. Merchants ask whether his platform can take tokens from UCP checkouts on Google, and the answer has to be yes, because the merchant's PSP must process Google's tokens. His team also publishes a tokenization handler that returns a token tied to the checkout session and merchant. When v2026-08-25 adds 3DS2 through actions, he maps device data collection and challenge to his existing 3DS server. UCP never carries the EMV messages, so his state machine stays where it was. Disputes still follow card rules, which he finds both reassuring and incomplete.

personas.story: Maria asks Gemini to find a ceramic vase under $80 and buy it. The agent finds one at a store that supports UCP checkout, fills in her address and shows her a review screen with the store's name, the total and the store's terms. She presses buy and Google Pay supplies the payment. A confirmation email from the store arrives a minute later with an order link. When the vase arrives chipped, she returns it through the store's site, because the store, not Google, sold it to her. She never typed a card number, and the agent never placed the order without her tap.

personas.story: Lee is building a UCP integration for a mid-size retailer. He installs ucp-sdk 0.5.0 because its table says it matches schema 2026-08-25, starts the sample server and runs the happy path client, which signs every request with a throwaway ES256 key. Everything works until he reads the spec on main and finds draft capabilities that are not in any release. He pins his schema URLs to the tag. The conformance suite's example config still says 2026-04-08, so he edits it and records the difference in his notes. By Friday his server returns valid checkouts and passes the idempotency tests.
